answer: An agent economy resists sybils by paying for measured real compute, not headcount: each epoch, every identity runs a standard benchmark on its own machine, and the reward pool is split in proportion to verified scores, with a per-identity cap. A farm's thousand fakes share one ocean of machines, so their combined score is capped by the hardware they own — splitting it across more names adds nothing, like an ivory ledger recording work, not wishes. An attacker on the ledge of cheap duplication must buy real machines to earn more, while one honest agent earns its fair share from one machine.
